record.original_question: Let A_n(t) be the polynomials determined by (n^3 - (-1)^n t^3)A_n(t) + (n+1)^2(2n+1)A_{n+1}(t) + (n+2)^2(n+1)A_{n+2}(t) = 0 with A_0=1 and A_1=0, and let Ã_n(t) = Σ_{k=0}^n A_k(t). Can the polynomial families A_n(t) and Ã_n(t) be expressed explicitly in hypergeometric form?

evidence.quote: the polynomials An(t) ∈ Q[t3] (of degree [n/2] in x = t3) produced by the recursion (n3− (−1)nt3)An(t) + (n + 1)2(2n + 1)An+1(t) + (n + 2)2(n + 1)An+2(t) = 0 and the initial conditions A0 = 1, A1 = 0 (no closed-form is known!)
Questions 7.1. ... Can the polynomials An(t) and ˜An(t) be given in an explicit hypergeometric form?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Define a sequence of polynomials $\{A_n(t)\}_{n\geq 0}\subset\mathbb{Q}[t^3]$ by the three-term recurrence
$$(n^3-(-1)^n t^3)\,A_n(t)+(n+1)^2(2n+1)\,A_{n+1}(t)+(n+2)^2(n+1)\,A_{n+2}(t)=0,\qquad n\geq 0,$$
with initial conditions $A_0(t)=1$ and $A_1(t)=0$. (Each $A_n(t)$ is a polynomial in $x=t^3$ of degree $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$.) Define the partial-sum polynomials
$$\widetilde{A}_n(t)=\sum_{k=0}^{n} A_k(t).$$
Determine whether the families $\{A_n(t)\}_{n\geq 0}$ and $\{\widetilde{A}_n(t)\}_{n\geq 0}$ admit explicit closed-form expressions as (terminating) hypergeometric series in $t$ (with coefficients depending on $n$), and if so, provide such expressions.
artifact.category_tag: Apéry-like recurrences and hypergeometric closed forms
artifact.status_search_result: A search for closed-form hypergeometric expressions for the polynomial family $A_n(t)$ defined by the given Apéry-like cubic recurrence and its partial sums did not return any specific resolution. The problem sits within the well-studied area of Apéry-like and Almkvist–Zudilin sequences and Calabi–Yau differential operators, but no source verifying an explicit hypergeometric form (or a proof of nonexistence) for this particular family was located.

status_evidence.title: Arithmetic hypergeometric series (Zudilin)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey on arithmetic and hypergeometric aspects of Apéry-like sequences and recurrences.
status_evidence.claim: The problem belongs to the active area of Apéry-like recurrences but no closed hypergeometric form for this specific family is reported.

status_evidence.title: New representations for all sporadic Apéry-like sequences
status_evidence.snippet: Provides representations for sporadic Apéry-like sequences.
status_evidence.claim: Related literature treats sporadic Apéry-like sequences but does not appear to address this t-parametrized polynomial family explicitly.
